questions.question: $\overrightarrow{OA}=\begin{pmatrix}5\\-2\end{pmatrix}$ and $\overrightarrow{OB}=\begin{pmatrix}-3\\4\end{pmatrix}$. What is the direction of $\overrightarrow{AB}$ (from the positive $x$-axis) to the nearest degree?
Mathematical induction is a method of proof that can be used to prove a statement:
options: for all integers $n\ge$ any fixed integer
questions.answer: **B.** The base case may be any fixed integer. (The school also accepted the first option.)

questions.question: For $f(x)=(x+3)(x-1)$, which represents the graph shown?
questions.answer: **D.** The graph is symmetric in both axes and exists only for $|x|\ge1$.

questions.question: Which integral gives the volume of a cone?
questions.answer: **C.** The radius $2-x$ is linear and reaches zero at an endpoint.

questions.question: If $X\sim B\left(4,\frac58\right)$, find $P(X=3)$.
Which is **not** a first-order linear differential equation?
A particle projected at speed $V$ has $\mathbf r=40t\,\mathbf i+\left(9t-\frac12gt^2\right)\mathbf j$. Which is correct?
If $\text{proj}_{\mathbf q}\mathbf p=\mathbf r$, what is $\text{proj}_{3\mathbf q}6\mathbf p$?
questions.answer: **C.** Scaling the target vector changes nothing; scaling the projected vector by 6 scales the result by 6.

questions.question: Find $\displaystyle\int\tan x\sec^2x\,dx$.
Which differential equation could match the slope field?
questions.answer: **D.** Slopes are zero on $y=0$ and vertical near $y=-x$.

questions.question: Solve $\dfrac{4-x^2}{x-1}\le0$.
A committee of 7 is chosen from 6 men and 8 women and must have exactly 4 men. How many committees are possible?
Forces of 80 N at 290°T, 110 N at 040°T and 90 N at 180°T act on an object. Show that the resultant is approximately $-4.5\mathbf i+21.6\mathbf j$ ($\mathbf i$ east, $\mathbf j$ north).
questions.answer:
$\mathbf F_1=(-80\cos20^\circ,\ 80\sin20^\circ)$, $\mathbf F_2=(110\cos50^\circ,\ 110\sin50^\circ)$, $\mathbf F_3=(0,-90)$.

Adding: $\mathbf F\approx-4.5\mathbf i+21.6\mathbf j$ N.

questions.question: A binomial random variable $X$ has $E(X)=\frac23$ and $\text{Var}(X)=\frac59$. Calculate $P(X\ge1)$.
Solve $3\cos x+2\sin x=-3$ for $0\le x\le2\pi$, to 1 decimal place where necessary.
$\mathbf a=\overrightarrow{OA}$, $\mathbf n=\overrightarrow{ON}$ with $OA=4$, $ON=6$ and $\angle AON=30^\circ$. Find $\text{proj}_{\mathbf n}\mathbf a$ as a multiple of $\mathbf n$.
Find the area bounded by $y=x^2-6$ and $y=x$, which meet at $(3,3)$ and $(-2,-2)$.
Using $u=\ln x$, find $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\ln x}x\,dx$.
$P(x,y)$ lies on the circle of radius $r$ centred at the origin, with $A(-r,0)$ and $B(r,0)$. Prove using vectors that $\overrightarrow{AP}\perp\overrightarrow{BP}$.
Using $\cos(2\theta+\theta)$, prove $\cos3\theta=4\cos^3\theta-3\cos\theta$.
Using $x=\cos\theta$ and $\cos3\theta=4\cos^3\theta-3\cos\theta$, solve $8x^3-6x-\sqrt3=0$.
questions.answer: $\cos3\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt3}2$, so $3\theta=\frac\pi6,\frac{11\pi}6,\frac{13\pi}6,\dots$. The three distinct roots are $x=\cos\dfrac\pi{18},\ \cos\dfrac{11\pi}{18},\ \cos\dfrac{13\pi}{18}$.

questions.question: Explain why $y=\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x$ is a constant function.
Given that $\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x$ is constant, find the constant.
Trevor states that $n^2+3n$ is odd for all integers $n\ge1$. Show that if the statement is true for $n=k$ then it is true for $n=k+1$.
Trevor states that $n^2+3n$ is odd for all integers $n\ge1$. Is this true? Justify.
questions.answer: No. For $n=1$, $n^2+3n=4$ is even, so there is no base case (in fact $n(n+3)$ is always even).

questions.question: The region bounded by $y=6-x^2$ and $y=2$ is rotated about the $y$-axis. Find the exact volume.
Consider $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=xe^{-y}$. Explain why it has no constant solution.
questions.answer: A constant solution needs $\frac{dy}{dx}=0$ for all $x$, i.e. $xe^{-y}=0$ for all $x$. Since $e^{-y}\ne0$, this is impossible.

questions.question: Consider $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=xe^{-y}$. Solve it by separating variables.
questions.answer:
$\displaystyle\int e^y\,dy=\int x\,dx$, so $y=\ln\left(\dfrac{x^2}2+C\right)$, valid where $\dfrac{x^2}2+C>0$.

*Note: the school writes $\ln\left|\frac{x^2}2+C\right|$; the absolute value is incorrect since $e^y>0$.*

questions.question: Given the graph of $y=f(x)$, sketch $y=\dfrac1{f(x)}$ showing key features.
questions.answer: Vertical asymptote $x=0$; horizontal asymptotes $y=\frac12$ (as $x\to-\infty$) and $y=-\frac12$ (as $x\to\infty$). The curve is above $y=\frac12$ for $x<0$ and below $y=-\frac12$ for $x>0$.

questions.question: Prove by induction that $8(8^n-1)-7n$ is divisible by 49 for all integers $n\ge0$.

500 rabbits are released on an island and $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=\dfrac P{10}\left(1-\dfrac P{2000}\right)$ ($t$ in months). Given $\dfrac{20000}{P(2000-P)}=10\left(\dfrac1P+\dfrac1{2000-P}\right)$, show that $P=\dfrac{2000}{1+3e^{-t/10}}$.
questions.answer:
$10\displaystyle\int\left(\frac1P+\frac1{2000-P}\right)dP=\int dt$, so $\ln\dfrac{P}{2000-P}=\dfrac t{10}+C$.

At $t=0$, $P=500$: $e^C=\frac13$. So $3P=(2000-P)e^{t/10}$, giving $P=\dfrac{2000}{1+3e^{-t/10}}$.

questions.question: A stone is projected from level ground at speed $V$ and angle $\theta$. By integrating vectors, show $\mathbf v=V\cos\theta\,\mathbf i+(V\sin\theta-gt)\mathbf j$ and $\mathbf r=Vt\cos\theta\,\mathbf i+\left(Vt\sin\theta-\frac g2t^2\right)\mathbf j$.
questions.answer: $\mathbf a=-g\mathbf j$. Integrating with $\mathbf v(0)=(V\cos\theta,V\sin\theta)$ gives $\mathbf v$; integrating again with $\mathbf r(0)=\mathbf 0$ gives $\mathbf r$.

questions.question: A stone is projected from level ground at speed $V$ and angle $\theta$. Its maximum height is 8 m. Using $\mathbf r=Vt\cos\theta\,\mathbf i+\left(Vt\sin\theta-\frac g2t^2\right)\mathbf j$, show the range is $\sqrt{\dfrac{64}g(V^2-16g)}$.
questions.answer:
Maximum height $\dfrac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}=8$, so $\sin\theta=\dfrac{4\sqrt g}V$ and $\cos\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{V^2-16g}}V$.

Time of flight $=\dfrac{2V\sin\theta}g=\dfrac8{\sqrt g}$.

Range $=V\cos\theta\cdot\dfrac8{\sqrt g}=\sqrt{\dfrac{64}g(V^2-16g)}$.
